Hey there @vangorra, mind taking a look at this pull request as it has been labeled with an integration (`withings`) you are listed as a [code owner](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/dev/CODEOWNERS#L1441) for? Thanks!

<details>
<summary>Code owner commands</summary>


Code owners of `withings` can trigger bot actions by commenting:

- `@home-assistant close` Closes the pull request.
- `@home-assistant rename Awesome new title` Renames the pull request.
- `@home-assistant reopen` Reopen the pull request.
- `@home-assistant unassign withings` Removes the current integration label and assignees on the pull request, add the integration domain after the command.

</details>
There are two calls to `async_update_entry` in `__init__.py`. Should either of those trigger a reload? It doesn't look like it, but I wanted to be extra sure since its tagged for a patch release.

For the cloudhook function we don't need it, but for the initial migration-ish code we might need it, since there can be a really really small possibility someone did not have a webhook id in their config. Can I just reload and this code will stop running?

<!-- ReviewDrafterComment -->
Please take a look at the requested changes, and use the **Ready for review** button when you are done, thanks :+1:

[_Learn more about our pull request process._](https://developers.home-assistant.io/docs/review-process#prs-are-being-drafted-when-changes-are-needed)
Why tho? We return the URL either way. This is the only place where we access the cloudhook property in de config entry data. So from an integration perspective it doesn't matter if we reload or not

> For the cloudhook function we don't need it, but for the initial migration-ish code we might need it, since there can be a really really small possibility someone did not have a webhook id in their config. Can I just reload and this code will stop running?

We don't need to reload the config entry if we're in the process of setting up the config entry and haven't loaded any platforms yet. When we update the config entry data, it is updated live so any subsequent access during config entry setup will see the updated data.

> Why tho? We return the URL either way. This is the only place where we access the cloudhook property in de config entry data. So from an integration perspective it doesn't matter if we reload or not

If the config entry is loaded we should generally reload the config entry if we update the config entry data so that all setup logic that access the config entry data gets the correct data.

It may be the case that this particular item in the data doesn't have any users in platforms etc at the moment. But it is probably safest to reload anyway so we don't need to remember that detail if we change some logic in the future.

If we want to avoid a reload when we generate a new cloudhook url we need to move `CONF_CLOUDHOOK_URL` to the init module and maybe make `async_cloudhook_generate_url` protected, so that we make sure that nothing else should access this config entry data.
Right, gave it a shot. Is this what you are expecting?

issue_context.title: Withings Integration Goes Into Unknown State Every Day
issue_context.body:
### The problem

Every night one of my Withings bed sensors, when we wake up, goes from clear -> unavailable -> unknown and I can't figure out why. This worked fine prior to the changes in 2023.10. I have 2 withings bed sensors and a scale. The issue is happening with 1 bed sensor and is the same bed sensor every time.

### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

2023.10.0b6

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

2023.9.3

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant OS

### Integration causing the issue

withings

https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/withings/

I am checking the logs and I can't really figure out what it's trying to do. Did you have to reauth today?

For some reason it's trying to reload the integration, making it unknown again, as we don't store the last state.
Nope. No reauth. Just seems to have reloaded the integration on its own.
Let me try to see if I can reproduce this. Are you sure that the HASH3 in your log is different from the other URLs?
Yup, just double checked
Can you compare that value to the cloudhook urls stored in that cloud file in .storage and the config entry data in config_entries data file in .storage, are they equal?
Yes, everything matches. And this is still happening each morning.

I have some fixes in 2023.10.1, will be available in a few hours. Maybe the cause is some leftover events that aren't cancelled when the intergation reloads. Let's see if that fixes anything, otherwise we have to dig deeper.

This is interesting, yesterday I did some tests with manually called the webhook to see if it would go unavailable. It did not. In this case, I would not expect an update from withings.

I just stood on my scale, and experienced the same problem, everything went unavailable for a split second.

Downside, I still had a test version running and I had no debug logging on. I will try to see how I can reproduce this better.

I know this is not helpful but I am having this issue as well. 

When I woke up to pee, the sensor went cleared (correct) but instantly went unavailable and after unknown. It didn't register occupancy after I went back. 

In the morning when I woke up the sensor registered clear again

![Screenshot_20231007-151517.png](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/assets/8025435/316215a1-502e-45f9-95bc-e3f346f10f69)
2023.10.1 did not fix the issue. @cdemi do you have two sleep sensors? Also are you on 2023.10.1?
I have only 1 sleep sensor. I updated to 2023.10.1 this morning. Will let you know tomorrow if I see any improvement
Interesting, so not sure what would be in common between the two of us. I assume also yours was working fine on 2023.9.x?
Correct, I've had this sensor up and running for at least 3 years. If it helps I'm not using Nabu Casa but I'm exposing my Home Assistant

Now that you gave the information that it didn't work the first time I might have a reason why this happens. I'll create a fix and if you could test it out, that'd be great.

Like the integration refreshes itself when an update to the configuration data happens. And getting a new token is also new configuration data. So my current guess is that the first time you got out of bed, it got a new access token and reloaded the integration.

```
cd /config
curl -o- -L https://gist.githubusercontent.com/bdraco/43f8043cb04b9838383fd71353e99b18/raw/core_integration_pr | bash /dev/stdin -d withings -p 101638
```
Could you maybe run this to run the changes as custom component?
I've installed this as a custom component. I'll report back tomorrow
Any updates?
I think that did it. Both sleep pads are in the correct state and this is the first time my morning automations worked on 2023.10
Aight, i'll put the PR ready for review
